cat << 'EOF' > model.py
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import lightgbm as lgb
from sklearn.metrics import mean_squared_error
import os

# Load data
print("Loading data...")
train_df = pd.read_csv('/app/data/train.csv')
val_df = pd.read_csv('/app/data/val.csv')
test_df = pd.read_csv('/app/data/test.csv')

# Separate target
target_col = 'target'
train_y = train_df[target_col]
train_x = train_df.drop(columns=[target_col])

val_y = val_df[target_col]
val_x = val_df.drop(columns=[target_col])

test_x = test_df

# Identify feature types
# num_ (numerical), bin_ (binary), cat_ (categorical)
# Since the task says missing numerical values are 'nan', 
# we should convert object columns to appropriate types.

print("Preprocessing features...")
for col in train_x.columns:
    if col.startswith('cat_'):
        train_x[col] = train_x[col].astype('category')
        val_x[col] = val_x[col].astype('category')
        test_x[col] = test_x[col].astype('category')
    elif col.startswith('bin_'):
        # Binary can be treated as numeric or categorical
        pass
    elif col.startswith('num_'):
        # Ensure numeric
        train_x[col] = pd.to_numeric(train_x[col], errors='coerce')
        val_x[col] = pd.to_numeric(val_x[col], errors='coerce')
        test_x[col] = pd.to_numeric(test_x[col], errors='coerce')

# LightGBM handles NaNs natively
print("Training LightGBM...")
params = {
    'objective': 'regression',
    'metric': 'rmse',
    'verbosity': -1,
    'boosting_type': 'gbdt',
    'random_state': 42,
    'learning_rate': 0.05,
    'num_leaves': 31,
}

dtrain = lgb.Dataset(train_x, label=train_y, categorical_feature=[c for c in train_x.columns if c.startswith('cat_')])
dval = lgb.Dataset(val_x, label=val_y, reference=dtrain, categorical_feature=[c for c in val_x.columns if c.startswith('cat_')])

model = lgb.train(
    params,
    dtrain,
    valid_sets=[dtrain, dval],
    valid_names=['train', 'valid'],
    num_boost_round=1000,
    callbacks=[lgb.early_stopping(stopping_rounds=50)]
)

print("Evaluating...")
preds_val = model.predict(val_x)
rmse = np.sqrt(mean_squared_error(val_y, preds_val))
print(f"Validation RMSE: {rmse}")

print("Predicting test set...")
test_preds = model.predict(test_x)

print("Saving predictions...")
output_df = pd.DataFrame({'target': test_preds})
output_df.to_csv('/app/predictions.csv', index=False)
print("Done!")
EOF
